item.text: {"item_id":"podcast:https://physicalaipodcast.co/episodes/009","version_id":"13aaf6bfc525bce0b9a1887162b0c0c3d4dd024b9bafd1c223a5bc48bd063692","decision":"accept","reason":"Relevant robotics context for physical-space systems: the episode reports a Tsinghua comparison of world-action-model designs and, at 00:07:28, limits most results to simulation while identifying one held-out real-robot task; it says code and weights are available at 00:07:35, giving builders a reproducibility path. It also provides timestamped, attributable evidence about what companies report checking: at 00:08:15, the host says Neura's founder described an uncut factory demo as about 60% autonomous, and at 00:09:22 proposes mean time between interventions as a more useful operational measure. The reported 70%, 6%, and 10% results are not independently verified here and automatic-transcript figures require checking against audio and the cited paper, so the item supports scrutiny of claimed checks rather than deployed-performance conclusions.","piece_ids":["01","02","03"]}
